m.description: Number of distinct item sizes (item types)

b.description: Number of items (demand) required for each item type

assumptions.description: There is at least one item type.
Every item size is a positive integer that does not exceed the bin capacity.

code.python: assert all(1 <= w[d] <= W for d in range(m))

assumptions.description: The demand for every item type is positive.

code.python: assert all(b[d] >= 1 for d in range(m))

A.description: Arc set of the graph G=(V,A) on vertices V={0,...,W}: item arcs (i, i+w_d) for every item type d and start vertex i, plus loss arcs (k, k+1) for every k=0,...,W-1.
A.formulation: A = \{(i, i + w_d) : d \in \{0, \ldots, m-1\},\; 0 \leq i \leq W - w_d\} \cup \{(k, k+1) : k \in \{0, \ldots, W-1\}\}

out.description: Adjacency list of outgoing arcs (arcs leaving each vertex)

inc.description: Adjacency list of incoming arcs (arcs entering each vertex)

D.description: Item arcs of each item type
D.formulation: D_d = \{(k, k+w_d) : k \in \{0, \ldots, W - w_d\}\} \quad \forall d \in \{0, \ldots, m-1\}

x.description: Flow on arc (i,j) in A: the number of items of size j-i placed in any bin at a distance i from the beginning of the bin

z.description: Number of bins used (feedback arc flow from vertex W back to vertex 0)

constraints.description: Flow conservation at vertex 0: inflow minus outflow equals the negative of the number of bins used.

code.gurobipy:
model.addConstr(
    gp.quicksum(x[i, j] for (i, j) in inc[0])
    - gp.quicksum(x[i, j] for (i, j) in out[0])
    == -z
)

constraints.description: Flow conservation at every intermediate vertex: inflow equals outflow.
Flow conservation at vertex W: inflow minus outflow equals the number of bins used.

code.gurobipy:
model.addConstr(
    gp.quicksum(x[i, j] for (i, j) in inc[W])
    - gp.quicksum(x[i, j] for (i, j) in out[W])
    == z
)

constraints.description: The full demand of every item type must be packed.

code.gurobipy: model.addConstrs(x[i, j] >= 0 for (i, j) in A)

constraints.description: The number of bins used doesn't exceed the total number of items.

objective.description: Minimize the total number of bins used.

notes: This is the arc-flow MILP formulation based on Equations 7-11 of carvalho1999 (with one added bound on z, noted below). Arcs $(i,j) \in A$ are indexed directly by their vertex pair, not by a separate item-type tag: $A$ is a plain set of pairs, formed as a union of the item-arc set and the loss-arc set.

A consequence of $A$ being a set of vertex pairs (inherited directly from the source, not introduced by this dataset): if some item type has width exactly 1, its item arc $(k,k+1)$ coincides with the loss arc $(k,k+1)$, and the same flow variable $x_{k,k+1}$ represents both a possible size-1 item placement and possible wasted capacity at that position. carvalho1999 does not address this case separately; we do not either, to stay faithful to Equations 7-11.

The bound $z \leq \sum_d b_d$ is not present in carvalho1999's Equations 7-11; it is added here because vertex 0 has no incoming arcs and vertex W has no outgoing arcs, so a pure-loss path $0 \to 1 \to \cdots \to W$ can carry arbitrarily large flow, leaving z otherwise unbounded above. The bound never excludes an optimal solution. This mirrors the analogous total-usage bound added to formulation `b`.
